c1-5-001.gate_key: adv_can | C1 | mcq | Which sentence has a mistake? | Last night the children could stay up until eleven.

key.correct: Last night the children could stay up until eleven.
wrong: We could stay up late on Saturdays when we were kids.
We couldn't go out on school nights.
In the end we were allowed to leave early.

item.why: Permission on one occasion: *were allowed to*, not *could*: *Last night the children were allowed to stay up until eleven.* *could* is for permission that was always there, and *couldn't* is fine for both.
item.why_lv: Atļauja vienā reizē: *were allowed to*, nevis *could*: *Last night the children were allowed to stay up until eleven.* *could* ir atļaujai, kas bija vienmēr, un *couldn't* der abos gadījumos.
item.correct: Last night the children could stay up until eleven.
wrong: We could stay up late on Saturdays when we were kids.
We couldn't go out on school nights.
In the end we were allowed to leave early.

c1-5-002.gate_key: adv_can | C1 | mcq | Choose the correct option: After driving round for three hours, we ___ find a parking space. | were able to

wrong: could
can
have been able to

item.q: Choose the correct option: After driving round for three hours, we ___ find a parking space.
item.why: One success on one past occasion: *were able to* (or *managed to*), not *could*: *we were able to find a parking space*.
item.why_lv: Viens *izdevies* mēģinājums pagātnē: *were able to* (vai *managed to*), nevis *could*: *we were able to find a parking space*.
wrong: could
can
have been able to

c1-5-003.gate_key: adv_can | C1 | mcq | Which sentence has a mistake? | The forms are able to be filled in online.

key.correct: The forms are able to be filled in online.
wrong: I could hear the sea from my hotel room.
We were able to finish the job on time.
She'll be able to drive next year.

item.why: Before a passive, use *can*: *The forms can be filled in online*, not *are able to be*.
item.why_lv: Pirms ciešamās kārtas lieto *can*: *The forms can be filled in online*, nevis *are able to be*.
item.correct: The forms are able to be filled in online.
wrong: I could hear the sea from my hotel room.
We were able to finish the job on time.
She'll be able to drive next year.

c1-5-004.gate_key: adv_can | C1 | mcq | Which sentence has a mistake? | May the figures in the report be wrong?

key.correct: May the figures in the report be wrong?
wrong: The results may point to a wider problem.
Could the figures be wrong?
Is she likely to accept the offer?

item.why: We don't ask about possibility with *May…?*: *Could the figures be wrong?* or *Are the figures likely to be wrong?*
item.why_lv: Par iespējamību nejautā ar *May*…?: *Could the figures be wrong?* vai *Are the figures likely to be wrong?*
item.correct: May the figures in the report be wrong?
wrong: The results may point to a wider problem.
Could the figures be wrong?
Is she likely to accept the offer?

c1-5-005.gate_key: adv_can | C1 | gap | Write one word in each gap: The next bus is in an hour, so we ___ as ___ walk. |

item.q: Write one word in each gap: The next bus is in an hour, so we ___ as ___ walk.
item.why: *might / may as well* + base verb = it is the only sensible thing to do: *we might as well walk*.
item.why_lv: *might / may as well* + pamatforma = tas ir vienīgais saprātīgais: *we might as well walk*.

c1-5-006.gate_key: adv_can | C1 | gap | You ___ me you were bringing five friends! I would have made more food. (might / warn) |

item.q: You ___ me you were bringing five friends! I would have made more food. (might / warn)
item.why: *You might have* + past participle: you should have done it (a reproach): *You might have warned me!*
item.why_lv: *You might have* + 3. forma: *tev* vajadzēja to izdarīt (pārmetums): *You might have warned me!*

c1-5-007.gate_key: adv_can | C1 | gap | This time next week I ___ on a beach in Crete. (may / lie) |

item.q: This time next week I ___ on a beach in Crete. (may / lie)
item.why: A possible activity at a future moment: *may be* + *-ing*, *I may be lying on a beach*.
item.why_lv: Iespējama darbība nākotnes brīdī: *may be + -ing, I may be lying on a beach*.

c1-5-008.gate_key: adv_can | C1 | gap | He didn't sound serious about leaving. He ___ . (might / joke) |

item.q: He didn't sound serious about leaving. He ___ . (might / joke)
item.why: A possible activity in the past: *might have been* + *-ing*, *he might have been joking*.
item.why_lv: Iespējama darbība pagātnē: *might have been + -ing, he might have been joking*.

c1-5-009.gate_key: adv_can | C1 | mcq | Choose the correct option: Winters here ___ very long, so bring warm clothes. | can be

wrong: can being
are able to be
could have been

item.q: Choose the correct option: Winters here ___ very long, so bring warm clothes.
item.why: *can* for what is sometimes or typically true: *Winters here can be very long.*
item.why_lv: *can* tam, kas mēdz būt vai ir raksturīgi: *Winters here can be very long.*
wrong: can being
are able to be
could have been

c1-5-010.gate_key: adv_subj | C1 | mcq | Which sentence has a mistake? | The board demanded the director to resign.

key.correct: The board demanded the director to resign.
wrong: The doctor recommended that she rest for a week.
I insist that he be told the truth.
They suggested that we should leave early.

item.why: *demand* is not followed by an object + *to*: *The board demanded that the director resign* (or *should resign*).
item.why_lv: Aiz *demand* nelieto *objektu + to*: *The board demanded that the director resign* (vai *should resign*).
item.correct: The board demanded the director to resign.
wrong: The doctor recommended that she rest for a week.
I insist that he be told the truth.
They suggested that we should leave early.

c1-5-011.gate_key: adv_subj | C1 | gap | We recommend that this medicine ___ taken with alcohol. (not / be) |

item.q: We recommend that this medicine ___ taken with alcohol. (not / be)
item.why: Formal: *not* + base form: *that this medicine not be taken*; also *should not be*, or *is not* in less formal English.
item.why_lv: Oficiāli: *not* + pamatforma: *that this medicine not be taken*; arī *should not be* vai mazāk oficiāli *is not*.

c1-5-012.gate_key: adv_subj | C1 | gap | It's odd that she ___ that. She's usually so polite. (should / say) |

item.q: It's odd that she ___ that. She's usually so polite. (should / say)
item.why: After *It's odd / surprising that*, *should* + verb shows surprise: *It's odd that she should say that.*
item.why_lv: Aiz *It's odd / surprising that should* + darbības vārds *izsaka* pārsteigumu: *It's odd that she should say that.*

c1-5-013.gate_key: adv_subj | C1 | gap | If the bank ___ to refuse the loan, we would sell the car. (be) |

item.q: If the bank ___ to refuse the loan, we would sell the car. (be)
item.why: *If* + *were to* for an unlikely future: *If the bank were to refuse…* (*was* is informal). Not *would* after *if*.
item.why_lv: *If + were to* maz *ticamai* nākotnei: *If the bank were to refuse*… (*was* ir sarunvalodā). Aiz *if* nelieto *would*.

c1-5-014.gate_key: adv_subj | C1 | mcq | Which sentence has a mistake? | If the bank would refuse, we would sell the car.

key.correct: If the bank would refuse, we would sell the car.
wrong: I wish it were Friday already.
If I were you, I'd take the job.
She speaks to me as if I were a child.

item.why: After *if*, not *would* for a condition: *If the bank refused / were to refuse, we would sell the car.*
item.why_lv: Aiz *if* nosacījumam nelieto *would*: *If the bank refused / were to refuse, we would sell the car.*
item.correct: If the bank would refuse, we would sell the car.
wrong: I wish it were Friday already.
If I were you, I'd take the job.
She speaks to me as if I were a child.

c1-5-015.gate_key: adv_subj | C1 | gap | I'd rather you ___ me before the meeting, not after it. (tell) |

item.q: I'd rather you ___ me before the meeting, not after it. (tell)
item.why: Something someone did in the past that you wish were different: *I'd rather you had told me.* *I'd rather you told me* is about now or later.
item.why_lv: Kaut kas, ko kāds izdarīja pagātnē un ko gribētos citādi: *I'd rather you had told me.* *I'd rather you told me* ir par tagadni vai nākotni.

c1-5-016.gate_key: adv_subj | C1 | mcq | Choose the correct option: The plan has its problems. ___, it's the best one we have. | Be that as it may

wrong: Be that as it is
Being that as it may
Be it as that may

item.q: Choose the correct option: The plan has its problems. ___, it's the best one we have.
item.why: A fixed phrase with the old subjunctive: *Be that as it may* = even so.
item.why_lv: Nemainīgs *izteiciens* ar *seno* konjunktīvu: *Be that as it may* = tomēr, lai kā arī būtu.
wrong: Be that as it is
Being that as it may
Be it as that may

c1-5-017.gate_key: adv_will | C1 | mcq | Choose the correct option: Keep the receipt in case you ___ to return the shoes. | should need

would need
had needed

item.q: Choose the correct option: Keep the receipt in case you ___ to return the shoes.
item.why: *in case* + *should* (or the present simple) for a small chance: *in case you should need to return them*, not *will*.
item.why_lv: *in case + should* (vai Present Simple) *nelielai* iespējai: *in case you should need to return them*, nevis *will*.
wrong: will need
